claim: Agentic workflows iteratively plan, call tools, evaluate results and correct themselves in a loop.
quote: An agentic workflow is a dynamic, AI-driven process in which one or more autonomous AI agents iteratively plan, reason, invoke external tools, and adapt their actions.

source_title: A practical guide to building agents (OpenAI)
quote: Applications that integrate LLMs but don't use them to control workflow execution—think simple chatbots, single-turn LLMs, or sentiment classifiers—are not agents.

claim: An agent is a model given tools it can call.
quote: The basic building block of agentic systems is an LLM enhanced with augmentations such as retrieval, tools, and memory.

claim: Tools let an agent take actions such as preparing an invitation or sending a message.

quote: Enable agents to interact with systems to take actions such as adding new information to databases, updating records, or sending messages.

claim: The difference between a chatbot and an agent is how the system is wired, not how intelligent the model is.
quote: Agents, on the other hand, are systems where LLMs dynamically direct their own processes and tool usage, maintaining control over how they accomplish tasks.

claim: An agent works in a loop: plan, use a tool, check the result, continue.

claim: Agents can take unintended actions, which is why guardrails are added from real failures.

quote: Add new guardrails based on real-world edge cases and failures you encounter.

claim: Sensitive or irreversible actions should stop for human oversight and approval.

claim: An agent picks its tools as the work changes, always inside defined guardrails.

claim: The browser asks DNS for the real address of the server the site lives on.
quote: The browser goes to the DNS server and finds the real address of the server that the website lives on.

claim: DNS matches a name you type to the IP address the browser needs.
quote: DNS translates domain names to IP addresses so browsers can load Internet resources.

claim: DNS behaves like an address book for websites.
quote: The Domain Name System (DNS) is like an address book for websites.

claim: Looking a name up is like looking up a contact before you call.
quote: An IP address is given to each device on the Internet, and that address is necessary to find the appropriate Internet device - like a street address is used to find a particular home.

claim: The browser then sends an HTTP request to that server, over the connection, using TCP/IP.
quote: The browser sends an HTTP request message to the server, asking it to send a copy of the website to the client. This message, and all other data sent between the client and the server, is sent across your internet connection using TCP/IP.

claim: HTTPS is HTTP with encryption between the client and the server.
quote: HTTPS (HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure) is an encrypted version of the HTTP protocol. It uses TLS to encrypt all communication between a client and a server.

claim: The reply is usually a bundle: HTML, CSS, JavaScript and media files.
quote: HTML files, which specify the web page content and its structure. CSS files, which specify styling and layout information. JavaScript files, which specify the behavior of interactive parts of the web page. Media assets such as images...

claim: The browser assembles the received files into the page: that process is rendering.
quote: This process of assembling the pieces into a web page is called rendering.

claim: Parsing HTML triggers further requests for stylesheets, scripts and media.
quote: Certain HTML elements, when parsed, will trigger more HTTP requests: elements referencing external CSS stylesheets;

claim: A page can be missing a tile and still show: the pieces arrive separately.
quote: The browser assembles the small chunks into a complete web page and displays it to you.

claim: Containers are how a web app's components are packaged and run in isolation.
quote: Simply put, containers are isolated processes for each of your app's components.

claim: A Docker image packages an application together with everything it needs to run.
quote: Self-contained. Each container has everything it needs to function with no reliance on any pre-installed dependencies on the host machine.

claim: An image is the packaged artefact; a container is that image running.
quote: A container image is a standardized package that includes all of the files, binaries, libraries, and configurations to run a container.

claim: Cloudflare sits between visitors and an origin server.
source_title: What is a WAF? (Cloudflare Learning Center)
quote: a WAF is a type of reverse-proxy, protecting the server from exposure by having clients pass through the WAF before reaching the server.

claim: A CDN keeps copies of content closer to users, and Cloudflare can also filter malicious traffic.
source_title: What is a CDN? (Cloudflare Learning Center)
quote: A content delivery network (CDN) is a geographically distributed group of servers that caches content close to end users.

claim: Cloudflare offers traffic filtering against attacks and unwanted traffic.
source_title: What is a WAF? (Cloudflare Learning Center)
quote: A WAF or web application firewall helps protect web applications by filtering and monitoring HTTP traffic between a web application and the Internet.

claim: Cloudflare is a network and security layer, not the host of your application.
source_title: What is a CDN? (Cloudflare Learning Center)
quote: While a CDN does not host content and can't replace the need for proper web hosting, it does help cache content at the network edge, which improves website performance.

claim: Docker isolates an application; security of the application is still the operator's job.
quote: There are four major areas to consider when reviewing Docker security: the intrinsic security of the kernel, the attack surface of the Docker daemon itself, loopholes in the container configuration profile, and the hardening security features of the kernel.
